name: remote-vnc
description: View and control a remote screen over VNC directly inside VS Code.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace, connections and pages saved in workspace settings are ignored; only user-level (global) ones are offered. Their preUseCommand/postUseCommand, which run arbitrary shell commands, are never honoured from workspace or folder settings unless the workspace is trusted.

remoteVnc.connections.markdownDescription: Saved VNC connections used by **Remote VNC: Connect to Saved Server…**.

host.description: Hostname or IP address of the VNC server.

username.description: Account name, for servers whose security type asks for one. macOS offers Apple ARD/DH ahead of VNC Auth and noVNC takes the first type it supports from the server's list, so a Mac target needs a username as well as a password. Leave unset for classic password-only servers, which ignore it.

port.description: TCP port of the VNC server (5900 + display number).

autoReconnect.description: Automatically reconnect (every 10s) if this connection drops unexpectedly. When omitted, the global "remoteVnc.autoReconnect" default applies.

forceRawEncoding.description: Compatibility mode: advertise only the Raw encoding and no desktop-resize pseudo-encodings. Enable for fixed-function embedded servers that render as a blank screen — their static framebuffer never reaches the viewer otherwise.

parkServerCursor.description: Park the server-drawn pointer in the bottom-right corner when idle — for touch-screen devices that paint a pointer arrow into the framebuffer. When omitted, the global "remoteVnc.parkServerCursor" default applies.

scaleViewport.description: Scale the framebuffer to fit the panel (true) or show it at its original 1:1 size with scrollbars (false). When omitted, the global "remoteVnc.scaleViewport" default applies.

visibleArea.description: Show only this WIDTHxHEIGHT area of the framebuffer (e.g. "480x272"). For servers that advertise a stride-padded framebuffer wider than the visible panel and render the padding as a dead black band. The "connected" line in the Remote VNC output logs the advertised size.

preUseCommand.markdownDescription: Shell command run BEFORE this connection is opened; the connection is only opened if it exits 0. **This executes an arbitrary shell command.** For entries that point at something that does not exist until it is started — a local dev server, a container, a device — so nothing has to be kept running all day for the entry to work. `${workspaceFolder}` and `${workspaceFolder:NAME}` are substituted; every other `${...}` is left for the shell. Runs in the first workspace folder. **Ignored** for entries saved in workspace or folder settings unless the workspace is trusted, because a cloned repository could otherwise run a command of its choosing the moment you open one of its entries; entries in your user settings are unaffected.

postUseCommand.markdownDescription: Shell command run when the LAST tab using this command closes, and when the window closes — the counterpart to `preUseCommand`, for taking the stack down again. **This executes an arbitrary shell command.** Started and not waited for, so it never delays closing a tab; its output goes to the "Remote VNC" output channel. Same `${workspaceFolder}` substitution and the same trust rule as `preUseCommand`: **ignored** for workspace- and folder-scoped entries unless the workspace is trusted.

preUseTimeout.markdownDescription: Seconds `preUseCommand` may run before it is given up on. On a timeout the command's whole process group is killed — not just the shell, so a build it started does not survive it — and the connection is not opened. Raise it for a command that has to build something on a cold cache.

remoteVnc.autoReconnect.markdownDescription: Reconnect automatically (every 10s) when a connection drops unexpectedly. A saved connection's own `autoReconnect` value overrides this default. Reconnecting always stops on authentication failure or a manual disconnect.

remoteVnc.parkServerCursor.markdownDescription: Park the server-drawn mouse pointer in the bottom-right corner after a few seconds of idle. For touch-screen devices whose VNC server paints a pointer arrow into the framebuffer — the arrow is pixels in the image, so it cannot be hidden client-side, only moved out of the way. Sends synthetic pointer moves (also in view-only mode). A saved connection's own `parkServerCursor` value overrides this default.

remoteVnc.screenshotDirectory.markdownDescription: Folder where **Remote VNC: Take Screenshot** saves PNG files and where recordings are saved without asking (`~` is expanded; the folder is created if missing). In a remote window (WSL, SSH, containers) this path is on the remote machine. Leave empty to pick a location every time.

remoteVnc.screenshotAction.markdownDescription: What happens when a screenshot is taken. `save` — write the file: silently into `remoteVnc.screenshotDirectory` when set, otherwise via a save dialog. `open` — stage the file in extension storage and open it as an editor tab without saving; a toast offers **Save As…**.

remoteVnc.screenshotCropEditor.markdownDescription: Which editor a screenshot opened by `remoteVnc.screenshotAction: "open"` lands in. `true` — the Remote VNC crop editor: drag a region over the capture and crop it in place. `false` — the built-in image preview. The crop editor stays reachable either way, through **Reopen Editor With…** and **Remote VNC: Crop Image…**.

remoteVnc.recordingFormat.markdownDescription: Format **Remote VNC: Start Recording** captures. `webm` — efficient video, fine for long recordings. `gif` — universally embeddable animation, 256 colours, large files; best for short clips.

remoteVnc.recordingFrameRate.description: Frames per second for recordings (both formats). Embedded panels update slowly — 10 is usually plenty and keeps GIF files small.

remoteVnc.recordingAction.markdownDescription: What happens when a recording stops. `save` — write the file like screenshots: silently into `remoteVnc.screenshotDirectory` when set, otherwise via a save dialog. `open` — stage the file in extension storage and open it as an editor tab without saving; a toast offers **Save As…**.

remoteVnc.viewOnly.description: Connect in view-only mode (ignore local keyboard and mouse input).

remoteVnc.scaleViewport.description: Scale the remote framebuffer to fit the editor panel.

remoteVnc.resizeSession.description: Request the server to resize the remote session to match the panel (if supported).

remoteVnc.qualityLevel.description: JPEG quality for the Tight encoding (0 = lowest, 9 = highest).

remoteVnc.compressionLevel.description: Compression level for the Tight encoding (0 = none, 9 = maximum).

remoteVnc.showDotCursor.description: Always show a small dot cursor, even when the server hides the pointer.

remoteVnc.bridgePort.markdownDescription: Fixed TCP port for the loopback `WebSocket ↔ TCP` bridge. Needed in a local Dev Container, where an ephemeral port is not forwarded automatically: set a port here and list the same one in `forwardPorts`. A fixed port allows only one session at a time. `0` picks an ephemeral port, which is correct everywhere else.

remoteVnc.controlServer.enabled.markdownDescription: Start a loopback HTTP API (`127.0.0.1`, random port) that lists open panels and captures screenshots and recordings of them, for driving the extension from a script or an agent. Off by default: enabling it opens a capture surface guarded only by a random token written to a file readable solely by this user (`control-<pid>.json` in this extension's global storage, one per window). It has no keyboard, mouse or navigation input routes — the only action beyond capture is reloading a page panel.

remoteVnc.pages.markdownDescription: Saved web pages opened as clean editor tabs by **Remote VNC: Open Web Page…** (e.g. design-mockup servers). Container-local `localhost` ports are forwarded automatically.

width.description: Optional fixed canvas width — with height set, the page renders at width×height scaled to fit the tab (design mockups). Omit for responsive pages.

height.description: Optional fixed canvas height (used together with width).

mirror.description: Render this page as a live mirror of a headless Chrome tab instead of an iframe. Costs a browser process and makes the tab a picture rather than a document (no text selection, no in-page find) — in exchange its pixels can be screenshotted and recorded. Falls back to the iframe when no browser is found.

preUseCommand.markdownDescription: Shell command run BEFORE this page is opened; the page is only opened if it exits 0. **This executes an arbitrary shell command.** For entries that point at something that does not exist until it is started — a local dev server, a container, a device — so nothing has to be kept running all day for the entry to work. `${workspaceFolder}` and `${workspaceFolder:NAME}` are substituted; every other `${...}` is left for the shell. Runs in the first workspace folder. **Ignored** for entries saved in workspace or folder settings unless the workspace is trusted, because a cloned repository could otherwise run a command of its choosing the moment you open one of its entries; entries in your user settings are unaffected.

postUseCommand.markdownDescription: Shell command run when the LAST tab using this command closes, and when the window closes — the counterpart to `preUseCommand`, for taking the stack down again. **This executes an arbitrary shell command.** Started and not waited for, so it never delays closing a tab; its output goes to the "Remote VNC" output channel. Same `${workspaceFolder}` substitution and the same trust rule as `preUseCommand`: **ignored** for workspace- and folder-scoped entries unless the workspace is trusted.

preUseTimeout.markdownDescription: Seconds `preUseCommand` may run before it is given up on. On a timeout the command's whole process group is killed — not just the shell, so a build it started does not survive it — and the page is not opened. Raise it for a command that has to build something on a cold cache.

remoteVnc.chromePath.markdownDescription: Browser binary used for pages saved with `mirror: true`. Leave empty to probe the usual locations for Chrome, Chromium and Edge — the DevTools protocol is the same for all three. In a remote window (WSL, SSH, containers) this path is on the remote machine, where the mirrored browser runs.

remoteVnc.mirrorFrameRate.markdownDescription: Approximate frames per second streamed from a mirrored page while you are actively using it (mouse, keyboard or wheel input in roughly the last 2 seconds). Approximate because Chrome takes a divisor of its own paint rate rather than a frame rate, and a page that paints less often sends less. Trade-off: a lower value costs less CPU; a higher value (up to 30, the default) cuts the keystroke-to-paint delay that otherwise makes a mirrored page feel laggy or stuck when you type or click into it. Once you stop interacting, the mirror drops to roughly a third of this rate automatically — there is no separate setting for that — and it stops streaming entirely while the tab is open but not focused, so the CPU cost of a high value is only paid while you are actually driving the page. Do not expect a low value to fix a hot mirrored tab by itself — measured on one animated page, capping brought CPU from 52% down to 34%, not lower, because most of that load is Chrome compositing the page's own animation, which no frame-rate setting removes.

remoteVnc.mirrorLaunchTimeout.markdownDescription: Seconds to wait for a mirrored page's headless Chrome to announce its DevTools endpoint before giving up and falling back to a plain (non-capturable) page. In practice this is a budget for a cold browser start, not a network timeout — a first launch also creates a browser profile, and on a memory-constrained machine (swap under pressure) that can take much longer than it does on an idle one. Raise it if mirroring reliably fails with "did not announce a DevTools endpoint" but a manually started Chrome does eventually come up.
